content.content:
### Cyrus v5: the owner's redesign (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v5`)

The owner's own Cyrus redesign (handoff `/tank/handoffs/cyrus/cyrus-handoff/`, START-HERE.md) replaces the v4 studio at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** (+ `/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`, and the core gallery at **`/dashboard/cyrus/cores`**). Same preview gate (`requireModBuilderUser()` on every page, `modBuilderUser()` on every API). The portal sidebar and top bar stay; the studio fills the app frame.

**Where it lives.** UI `components/cyrus/{chrome,cosmos,cores,icons,preview,prompt}` + `CyrusApp.tsx` (handoff components, imports re-rooted); state/engine `lib/cyrus/{store,forge,fx,data,types,camera,hooks,zip,highlight}.ts` + `lib/cyrus/engine/` (template generators); game logos `public/cyrus/games/`. Kept from v4: `components/cyrus/kit/` (icon set used by the token modal, the install-to-server modal), `lib/cyrus/{projects,meta,models,estimate,uploads,diff,tokens/}`.

**Scoping (nothing leaks into the portal).** `app/dashboard/cyrus/layout.tsx` wraps every Cyrus route in `.cyrus-root.nx-dark-island` and loads Inter / Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono as CSS variables on that box only. `studio.css` (handoff globals + network CSS) and `cores/cores.css` are generated from the handoff with every selector under `.cyrus-root`, keyframes and `@property` renamed `cy5-*`, and the three class names that collide with portal globals renamed (`cy5-glass`, `cy5-btn-ghost`, `cy5-kbd`). The root uses `container-type: size; contain: layout paint`, so the handoff's `position: fixed` chrome is contained in the content area; `100vw/vh` became `cqw/cqh`. Tailwind colour tokens are `cy-*` (`text-cy-ink`, `border-cy-line` …, `@theme inline` in `app/globals.css` pointing at variables that exist only on `.cyrus-root`), plus a `cy-light:` variant. `nx-dark-island` keeps the portal's generated light-mode retargeting off the studio (it has its own light theme). `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a studio selector is unscoped or a keyframe isn't `cy5-`.

**Theme.** The portal's: `html[data-theme="light"]` / localStorage `nx-theme`. The studio's toggle presses the portal's own toggle button; `useCyrusBoot` mirrors `data-theme` into the store for the canvas and shaders. No `cyrus-theme` key.

**Real vs template.** Minecraft is the one real game (`GAMES[].real`). The account's builds are its Minecraft mods (`lib/cyrus/real.ts deriveReal`: one mod per project, builds = versions, category from the build's own words, at most two extra category branches). Minecraft seeds are dashed **ideas**: clicking one writes a buildable prompt. Notes / restore / favourite are the existing `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root`; files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`; downloads are the real `.jar` / source zip; **Deploy** opens the v4 install modal. Every other game (and added games) is the handoff's template generator, labelled "Template preview", spends no tokens, kept in localStorage per account (`cyrus-state-v1:<userId>`).

**Forge stream** (`POST /api/cyrus/generate`, NDJSON, handoff §6 GenEvents). A prompt that routes to Minecraft, or a change to a real mod, goes through `lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild` (extracted from `POST /api/mod-builder/builds`, which now calls it too: same validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap and token gate); token errors answer JSON 402/403/429 before the stream so `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError` opens the modal. Then `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` streams the real build: stage changes → `think`, the service `/live` draft → `file`/`chunk`, in-place edits → `file-set`, keep-alive `ping`, final source + `done {tokens: charged}` or `error`. `GET ?follow=<id>` re-attaches (page load with a running build, dropped connection; the client retries 4×). Template games run the handoff's `forgeStream()` (no model call). Additive event types: `build`, `file-set`, `ping`.

**Tokens** (UI-CONTRACT.md): `<CyrusTokensHost/>` in `CyrusApp`; `<CyrusTokenChip compact/>` replaces the handoff's credit counter in the top bar; `<CyrusTokenEstimate/>` in the prompt dock for real targets; `<CyrusModelLock/>` + typical token range per model + `<CyrusModelPanelFoot/>` in the model picker; `cyrusTokens.refresh()` after each real build. The local `credits` counter is gone. Model ids/names stay the economy's: Katara / Saka / Yakko.

**Verification** (node-2, devhost): throwaway DB seeded by `.cyrus-verify/seed.ts` (not committed), a local stand-in of the build service (`.cyrus-verify/mock-svc.mjs`, same HTTP as the VM; the portal's real create/sync/live/source/jar code runs unchanged), Playwright screenshots in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-redesign/shots/`.

### Cyrus token economy (2026-10-07, branch `feature/cyrus-tokens`)

input.command:
cd /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-routing && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/DOCUMENTATION.md'
s=open(p).read()
anchor='### Cyrus token economy (2026-10-07, branch `feature/cyrus-tokens`)'
new='''### Cyrus v6: broad-request routing, universal categories, listing dialog (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v6-routing`)

**Routing (`lib/cyrus/route.ts`, pure, client-side, zero API calls).** `routeRequest(text, { selection, hover }, { games, projects })` returns a `RouteDecision { intent: create|refine|fix|explain|install|browse|unknown, gameId, categoryId, projectId?, confidence, reason, clarify?, unsupported?, via }`. Fast path only: game names/aliases (typo-tolerant: no typos under 5 letters so "trust" is never Rust, 1 up to 7, 2 beyond; aliases after the first two count as weak content words), `my|the <name> mod/plugin` fuzzy-matched against the account's own projects (plugin names count, "coinshop" = "Coin Shop", version suffixes ignored so "Frost Axe" vs "Frost Axe v2" is a tie), implicit title matches only with an action verb, intent verbs, universal category keywords. The selected (or hovered) mod/game is the context unless the text names another game or asks for a new mod. Ambiguity never calls a model: it returns `clarify` with one-tap options (which game, which mod, "no mod called X: did you mean…"), each a complete decision. Unsupported games (Skyrim, ARK, GTA, Bedrock…) are named plainly with the supported games offered. 80+ phrases in `test/cyrus-route.test.ts`; ~0.1 ms per call. `browse` is an addition to the brief's intents ("what mods do I have for Valheim").
**The dock** (`components/cyrus/prompt/{routing.ts,RouteChip.tsx}`, small hooks into `PromptDock`): the chip shows where the request goes while typing ("Creating a new Minecraft mod in Weapons", "Refining Coin Shop"); Enter acts: create = select game+category then forge, refine/fix = select the mod (camera glides, preview opens) then forge, explain = open the mod's notes (`EXPLAIN_TAB`, switch to studio-ui's Explain tab on merge), install = open the install modal (`cyrus:install` window event, `PreviewPanel` listens), browse = the game's overview. The real/template label and the token estimate follow the decision. Hover isn't wired yet (Network keeps it internally; `RouteContext.hover` is ready).

**Universal categories (`lib/cyrus/categories.ts`).** 16 stable ids, identical on every game: environment, creatures (Creatures & NPCs), weapons, items, magic, vehicles, gameplay, quests, minigames (Game modes), economy, admin, utility (Utility & QoL), interface, visuals, audio, performance. Each has label, blurb, accent, keywords, `store` (the NxLabs TaxKey it files under), `engine` (the template generator archetype) and `worldContent` (could disabling it remove world content, for the lifecycle/toggle policy). `normalizeCategory()` accepts every older id (v5 `worlds/characters/mechanics/shaders`, v4 `worldgen/biomes/structures/other`, plain words). Per game: `categoriesForGame(id, support?)` = the game's `GameSupport.categories` when present, else `DEFAULT_GAME_CATEGORIES`. `CategoryKey` in `lib/cyrus/types.ts` is unchanged: it is now explicitly the generators' archetype; the map/`Mod`/`Selection`/`Game.categories`/route events use `CyrusCategoryId`, and `lib/cyrus/data.ts engineMeta(id, text)` hands a generator its archetype labelled with the universal name. Icons: `components/cyrus/icons/CategoryIcons.tsx` (12 v5 glyphs re-used, 5 new: game modes, economy, admin, utility, performance; 24 px, `currentColor`, 1.6 stroke, duotone).
**Auto-sorter** `autoSort({ prompt, changes, title, summary, commands, permissions, config, files, allowed })`: deterministic, zero API: weighted keywords, command names (`/pay` economy, `/sethome` utility, `/ban` admin…), and loader API calls in the generated code (Bukkit/Paper, Oxide, BepInEx, tModLoader, Zomboid/UE4SS Lua); one primary + up to two secondaries, `confidence`, `confident`, and the evidence (`why`). Low confidence = the listing dialog asks the owner instead of guessing. Real projects: a saved category (`ModBuild.cyrus.category` on the root build, `categorySource: auto|owner`) is always used; otherwise `lib/cyrus/real.ts sortProject()` decides on the fly (map keeps at most two extra auto branches; overflow goes to the mod's best visible secondary, else Gameplay).
**Migration helper** `scripts/cyrus-categorize-projects.ts`: dry run by default; `--apply` stores the auto-sorted category on projects without one, refuses any DB that isn't a node-2 throwaway unless `CYRUS_MIGRATE_ALLOW_PROD=yes-the-owner-approved`. Not run on production.

**Listing (`lib/cyrus/listing.ts` contract, `lib/cyrus/listing-client.ts` adapter, `components/cyrus/listing/`).** `ModListingInput { title, categoryId, secondaryCategoryIds, iconAssetId|null, description }` + `validateListing`, `draftDescription` (free: from the build summary, 280 chars at a sentence), icon refs (`glyph:<category>`, `glyph:mono`, `local:<root>` for an upload, or an NxLabs asset id). The dialog opens by itself when a NEW mod finishes ("Name your mod", once) and from the pencil "Edit listing" in the preview header (own mods only). Category = auto-sorted (badge + evidence) with one-tap override; uploads are cropped in the browser to the rounded 128 px tile (WebP, ≤24 KB) and kept on the project until the NxLabs asset store exists. Storage today: real projects → `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root` (meta fields `category, secondaryCategories, categorySource, description, icon, iconData`, validated in `lib/cyrus/meta.ts`); template mods → the local mod + localStorage `cyrus-listings-v1`. **Merge note:** the community agent's `saveModListing` plugs into `COMMUNITY_BACKEND` in `listing-client.ts`.

'''
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor,new+anchor,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status 2>&1 | tail -6

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
**routing agent: finished.** Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-routing`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-routing`. Four commits on top of `feature/cyrus-v6`: dc28936aa2, cff4e1ec59, 043426d21a, 2aa0a20eb1. Nothing deployed, nothing merged, no production data touched. On node-2 the final `devhost tsc` is clean (exit 0) and 128 of 128 tests pass in `test/cyrus-route.test.ts`, `test/cyrus.test.ts` and `test/light-theme.test.ts`. `gen-light-literals --check` is up to date. My dev server and mock service are stopped.

**What I built**
- **A. Broad prompt routing** (`lib/cyrus/route.ts`, runs in the browser, no API calls).
  - It returns a `RouteDecision { intent, gameId, categoryId, projectId?, confidence, reason, clarify?, unsupported?, via }`.
  - It handles:
    - game names with typos (short words like "trust" never match Rust)
    - "my <name> mod" matched against the user's own projects, including plugin names ("coinshop" finds Coin Shop)
    - verbs that say what the user wants (make, fix, explain, install, show)
    - category keywords
  - It never calls a model when it is unsure. It shows one-tap choices instead, for example "Frost Axe or Frost Axe v2?", "Which game?", "No mod called X, did you mean…".
  - Unsupported games (Skyrim, ARK, GTA, Minecraft Bedrock) get a plain "Cyrus doesn't build X yet" plus the supported games.
  - I added one intent beyond the brief, `browse`, for "what mods do I have for Valheim".
  - In the dock (`components/cyrus/prompt/{routing.ts,RouteChip.tsx}`), a chip shows the destination while typing, e.g. "Creating a new Minecraft mod in Weapons". On Enter the camera flies there, the preview opens, and the forge starts. Explain opens the notes; install opens the install modal; browse opens the game overview.
  - The test file has 80+ phrases (typos, other word orders, several games named, "my mod" with 0, 1 or many matches). Each call takes about 0.1 ms.
- **B. 16 preset categories, the same for every game** (`lib/cyrus/categories.ts`):
  - The ids are environment, creatures, weapons, items, magic, vehicles, gameplay, quests, minigames, economy, admin, utility, interface, visuals, audio, performance.
  - Each one maps to an NxLabs store bucket, a template-generator type, and a "could disabling it remove world content" flag.
  - Old ids are converted automatically, both v5 ("worlds", "mechanics") and v4.
  - Each game has a default category list until its own support file lists them.
  - I drew 5 new SVG icons (game modes, economy, admin, utility, performance) and reused the other 12.
  - The auto-sorter costs no API calls. It reads the prompt, summary, command names, config and the generated code, and picks one main category plus up to two secondary. It reports how sure it is; when unsure, the dialog asks the owner instead of guessing.
  - `CategoryKey` is unchanged and still means the template generators' 12 types, so the game agents' generator files did not change. The map, mods and selections now use `CyrusCategoryId`.
  - Migration helper: `scripts/cyrus-categorize-projects.ts`. It is a dry run by default. `--apply` refuses any database that isn't a node-2 throwaway unless `CYRUS_MIGRATE_ALLOW_PROD=yes-the-owner-approved` is set; I tested that refusal. A dry run on seeded data sorted all 6 projects sensibly. I did not run it on production.
- **C. Listing dialog** (`components/cyrus/listing/`, contract in `lib/cyrus/listing.ts`, storage adapter in `lib/cyrus/listing-client.ts`):
  - It opens by itself once when a new mod finishes building ("Name your mod"). A pencil "Edit listing" button in the preview header reopens it for the user's own mods.
  - Fields:
    - title
    - category, auto-sorted with its evidence shown and easy to override
    - up to two extra categories
    - icon: category glyph, generated monogram, or an upload cropped in the browser to the rounded tile
    - 280-character description drafted for free from the build summary

**How I verified it**
I ran the real server-rendered `/dashboard/cyrus` on node-2 with a throwaway DB and a local stand-in for the build service. Pages returned 200 with no page errors and no sideways scroll at any size, in dark and light, at 1440 and 390. 31 screenshots are in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/routing/shots/`. They cover: create from the core with nothing selected, the clarify chips, an unsupported game, the refine jump, the explain jump, the listing dialog, an override and save, and the new-mod dialog appearing after a build. The seed script, shots script, migration dry run and `CATEGORIES.md` (a note for the other agents) are in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/routing/`. Docs are added to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

**Open items and merge notes**
- **Community agent:** plug `saveModListing` into `COMMUNITY_BACKEND` in `lib/cyrus/listing-client.ts`. Until then, real projects keep the listing on the project record (`PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root`), and template mods keep it in the browser. Uploaded icons are stored on the project as small inline images until the NxLabs asset store exists.
- **Studio agent:** when its Explain tab lands, change `EXPLAIN_TAB` in `components/cyrus/prompt/routing.ts` from "notes" to "explain". My edits to shared files are small: `PromptDock`, a pencil button and an install-event listener in `PreviewPanel`, and one line in `CyrusApp`.
- **Game agents:** any new generator code should key on `CategoryKey` (the 12 types). Support files should list the universal category ids; older names are converted.
- **Hover is not wired.** The router supports it, but the network keeps hover state internally.
- **`test/cyrus-mods.test.ts` fails** with a "server-only import" error. It fails the same way on the base branch, so it is not from this work.
- **Map change:** a game can now show up to 3 extra auto-sorted category branches (was 2), so common plugin types like economy, utility and performance keep their own branch.
- **The optional cheap-model fallback is designed but not built.** One-tap clarification replaces it, and nothing in routing or sorting spends API usage.

**Decisions for the owner**
1. Whether to approve running the category migration on production.
2. Whether the 16 category names and labels are right.
3. Whether "Creepers drop diamonds" should file under Creatures & NPCs (what the sorter picks now) or Items & gear.
